items.title: Mortgage Rates Edge Back Up to 6.66%; 15-Year at 5.98%, Jumbo Eases to ~6.71%
items.summary: Freddie Mac's Aug. 27 Primary Mortgage Market Survey put the 30-year fixed at 6.66%, one basis point above the prior week and up from 6.56% a year ago, snapping a two-week slide. The 15-year averaged 5.98%, up from 5.95%. Chief economist Sam Khater cited resilient consumer spending and rising household incomes, with more listings and slower price growth giving buyers better options and creating a more balanced market. The 30-year jumbo average moved the other way, easing roughly eight basis points on the week to about 6.71%, narrowing the jumbo-to-conforming spread to about five basis points.

items.title: Fairfield Buys West Palm Beach's 812-Unit Portofino Place From Cortland for $208M at ~$256,200 Per Door
items.summary: San Diego-based Fairfield Residential paid $208 million for the 812-unit Portofino Place Apartments at 4400 and 4600 Portofino Way in West Palm Beach, buying from Atlanta-based Cortland - about $256,200 per unit and the second-largest South Florida multifamily trade of the year. The 2003- and 2006-built complex spans 34 three-story buildings and two clubhouses on nearly 40 acres; Fairfield financed it with $93.1 million and $85 million Freddie Mac loans maturing in 2033. South Florida multifamily investment volume reached $2.5 billion in the first half, up 19.4% year over year per Avison Young, and in the 12 months through Q2 leasing (13,774 units) outpaced deliveries (12,751) for the first time in three years per CoStar - though average asking rents still slipped 1.3% year over year to $2,279 in July.

items.title: Midtown Capital Pays $86M for 14-Building Doral Industrial Portfolio at $296 PSF; Mana Wynwood Sale to Ken Griffin Reported at $700M-Plus
items.summary: Midtown Capital Partners acquired a 300,000-square-foot, 14-property small-bay industrial portfolio along Northwest 54th and 56th Streets and Northwest 79th and 82nd Avenues in Doral for $86 million - roughly $296 per square foot and a near-record for Miami-Dade - from 13 separate sellers tied to the Waas family, who developed and managed the buildings for decades. Miami industrial posted 402,000 square feet of positive net absorption in the second quarter, pulling vacancy to 6.9% with rents near record highs, per Avison Young. Separately, The Real Deal reports that Moishe Mana's 30-acre Mana Wynwood campus is being sold to billionaire Ken Griffin at a rumored $700 million to more than $1 billion, which would set a South Florida record for a development assemblage; neither party has confirmed the deal, and both denied it earlier this year.

items.title: Lost Tree Village Waterfront Teardown Trades for $27.5M - More Than $4,000 Per Foot in North Palm Beach
items.summary: The estate of the late Penn Corporation founder Dana Hamel sold 11800 Turtle Beach Road in North Palm Beach for $27.5 million, over $4,000 per square foot on a 6,800-square-foot home built in 1992. The property listed in April at $35 million; Hamel had paid $2.5 million for it in 1991. The buyer, shielded behind 11800 Turtle Beach Rd LLC, plans to tear down and rebuild on the roughly one-acre lot with 128 feet of water frontage. James Kenny and Paul Kaneb of K2 Realty had the listing and represented both sides. Lost Tree Village, a 450-acre community with a private oceanfront and golf course, set its record at $55 million last year.

items.title: Amendment 3 Would Lift Florida's Homestead Exemption to $250K and Cut $11.86B a Year From Local Tax Rolls
items.summary: The November ballot measure would raise Florida's homestead exemption from $50,000 today to $150,000 next year and $250,000 by 2028 for non-school property taxes, and halve the annual assessment-growth cap on non-homestead property — investment homes, second homes and commercial real estate — from 10% to 5%. State economists put the statewide revenue hit at $11.86 billion a year, with Miami-Dade losing an estimated $445 million and Broward $326 million annually by fiscal 2028-29. Three consolidated lawsuits forced a court-ordered rewrite of the ballot language, and University of North Florida polling showed support sliding from 61% to 45% once voters were told the budget impact — well under the 60% threshold required to pass.

items.title: 25-Story Live Local Act Tower Filed in Downtown West Palm Beach — 40% Workforce Housing, 60% Condos
items.summary: Urban Design Studio and Arquitectonica submitted a pre-application for a 25-story tower at 215 Fifth Street in downtown West Palm Beach: 36 workforce-housing rentals on the second and third floors and 41 market-rate condos above, including an 8,500-square-foot penthouse, with a fourth-floor amenity deck and pool. The developer has not been identified; the vacant 1920s commercial site last sold in 2005 for $5.9 million to an entity tied to Marsha Stocker, daughter of the late Palm Beach landlord Burt Handelsman. The Live Local Act, signed in 2023 and expanded this year, grants tax breaks and lets developers bypass municipal approval when at least 40% of units are workforce or affordable. Steve Ross and Jeff Greene have both filed Live Local projects nearby.

items.title: Whole Foods-Anchored Doral Marketplace Trades for $83M at $1,056 Per Square Foot
items.summary: An entity managed by Jonathan Perlman, founder and CEO of Dallas-based Tradition Senior Living, bought the newly completed 78,600-square-foot Doral Marketplace at Northwest 41st Street and Northwest 107th Avenue from Atlanta-based SJC Ventures, assuming the seller's $50.1 million loan, which was reassigned to Bank of Texas. The 8.2-acre center holds a 38,000-square-foot Whole Foods plus 40,700 square feet of strip retail and 488 parking spaces. SJC and Nuveen paid $32 million for the site in 2024 and delivered the project this year. Grocery-anchored retail keeps clearing steadily in South Florida: Nuveen paid $46.3 million for Aldi-anchored Coral Landings III in Margate in April, and Publix bought Fountains of Boynton for $78 million in May.

items.title: Una Residences Penthouse Sells for $17.9M at $2,700 PSF; Key Biscayne Waterfront Trades at $3,300 PSF
items.summary: A trust paid $17.9 million for a 6,200-square-foot penthouse at Una Residences, 175 Southeast 25th Road in Brickell, developed by OKO Group and Cain — $2,700 per square foot and the day's priciest recorded South Florida home sale. In Key Biscayne, 591 North Mashta Drive sold for $14.3 million, or $3,300 per square foot, from a company managed by Alvaro Castro Mendivil to Isabela Ribaudo; the 4,300-square-foot house last traded at $3.2 million in 2004 and was asking just under $17 million in January (Cristina Anglemont De Tassigny of EXP Realty had the listing, Giulietta Ulloa of BHHS EWM Realty brought the buyer). A three-bedroom at Five Park, 501 West Avenue in Miami Beach, fetched $8.5 million, or $3,400 per square foot, up from $7 million in 2024.

items.title: Palm Beach Billionaires' Row Estate Lists for $195M — A Sale at Ask Would Set an Island Record
items.summary: A rebuilt-from-scratch lake-to-ocean estate at 1616 South Ocean Boulevard hit the market at $195 million, roughly $9,790 per square foot. The nearly 20,000-square-foot, 7-bedroom/12.5-bath home sits on almost two acres with both Intracoastal and Atlantic frontage and an 18-car garage; it was reconstructed in 2023. Christian Angle Real Estate has the listing. The property last traded at $22.4 million in 2018 and was owned by former Avis CEO Joseph Vittoria, who paid about $5.7 million in 1996. A sale at ask would eclipse the island's $170 million record set in 2023 at 589 North County Road. Angle also holds a $205 million former Gucci-heir compound, and a 2.25-acre estate at 911 North Ocean Boulevard has been asking $185 million since November.

items.title: Design District Commercial Condo Trades for $17.3M at $680 PSF; Miami Industrial and Palm Springs School Also Close
items.summary: Alta Developers sold a 25,500-square-foot commercial condo at the Quadro, 3900 Biscayne Boulevard in Miami's Design District, for $17.3 million — about $680 per square foot — to Hollywood-based JBL Asset Management; Alta completed the 12-story project in 2019. Also recorded: a 10,300-square-foot industrial complex at 6400 Northwest 84th Avenue in Miami for $6.5 million, sold by an Alan Leibowitz entity to an affiliate of Roberts Oxygen Company after trading at $4.8 million in 2024; and the 9,900-square-foot Kingswood Academy early-childhood center at 4137 South Congress Avenue in Palm Springs for just under $6 million on a 2.4-acre lot.

items.title: Apartment Property Insurance Up 58% in Five Years — The Fastest-Growing Landlord Expense, Trepp Finds
items.summary: Property insurance has climbed 58 percent over the past five years, making it the fastest-growing major operating-expense line for apartment owners, according to new research from Trepp cited by The Real Deal. With rent growth decelerating, the increase lands directly on net operating income — and on the cap rates buyers are willing to underwrite. The pressure is sharpest in coastal Florida, where premiums have run well above national averages, though Citizens' 2026 rate reductions and softer reinsurance pricing have begun to ease the trend on the residential side.

items.title: Palm Beach Lakefront Estate Sells for $26.5M - 1,458% Above Its 2005 Price
items.summary: A lakefront house at 127 Ocean View Road in Palm Beach's Estate Section, about a mile south of Mar-a-Lago, traded for a recorded $26.5 million after more than 25 years in the same family. Heidi Niblack and retired pharmaceutical executive John Niblack sold as co-trustees of a revocable trust; the buyer was Florida Iconic Ventures LLC, managed by Issac Ashkenazy and sharing an address with New York-based Ashkenazy Acquisition Corp. The 1999-built, four-bedroom house has 8,387 square feet inside and out plus a lakefront pool and spa. The sellers paid $1.7 million in 2005 for the house and an oceanfront parcel down the street - a 1,458% gain.
items.source: Palm Beach Daily News via Boca Raton Tribune

items.title: Miami Beach Double-Lot Mansion Trades for $51.5M; Al Capone's Former Palm Island Lot Fetches $21M
items.summary: A trust paid $51.5 million for the newly built waterfront mansion at 270 South Hibiscus Drive in Miami Beach, off a $55 million ask. The seller was an entity managed by broker Denis Smykalov; the 10,500-square-foot, seven-bedroom house sits on a double lot. Jordan Karp had the listing and Dora Puig of Luxe Living Realty represented the buyer. Separately, the 30,000-square-foot waterfront lot at 93 Palm Avenue that once held Al Capone's mansion sold for $21 million to an LLC tied to Russian businessman Ilya Karpov, up from $15.5 million in 2021.

items.title: Brickell Development Site Sells for $50M for Planned 60-Story Tower; SW Miami-Dade Industrial Trades at $24.5M
items.summary: Prosper Group and Versluys Group paid $50 million for a Brickell assemblage - two commercial buildings totaling 16,800 square feet at 625 SW First Avenue and 66 SW Sixth Street plus a 74,400-square-foot vacant lot at 99 SW Seventh Street - from Two Roads Development and Newgard Development Group. The buyers are planning a 60-story residential tower on the site. In southwest Miami-Dade, a 155,000-square-foot two-story industrial building and parking lot at 11900-11905 SW 128th Street changed hands for $24.5 million.

items.title: Mortgage Rates Fall a Second Straight Week to 6.65%; 15-Year Dips to 5.95%
items.summary: Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey put the 30-year fixed at 6.65% for the week ending August 20, down from 6.67% and the second consecutive weekly decline. The 15-year fixed eased to 5.95% from 5.96%. Both sit modestly above year-ago levels of 6.58% and 5.69%. Jumbo 30-year pricing averaged roughly 6.78%, down from about 6.84% in mid-August - the more relevant benchmark for most South Florida coastal and luxury purchases, where loan sizes clear the $832,750 conforming ceiling.

items.title: Russian Businessman Sells Miami Beach's 2740 North Bay Road Lot for $72M, More Than Triple His 2022 Price
items.summary: Ilyha Karpov sold the vacant 0.6-acre waterfront lot at 2740 North Bay Road in Miami Beach to a trust for $72 million - the week's priciest recorded South Florida residential deal. Karpov had paid $20.8 million for the site in 2022, buying from Delphine Dray, owner of Miami Beach's National Hotel. The top commercial trade was in Miami Beach as well: an affiliate of Coral Gables-based Capital Realty Services sold the 31,000 SF two-story mixed-use building at 1200 Washington Avenue for $10 million, or about $323 per square foot, to an entity managed by investor Ryan Manoocheri; the property last traded for $2.8 million more than two decades ago. Also recorded: the estate of Rudolf Silk sold a 42,000 SF West Palm Beach industrial property at 2658-2660 Electronics Way for $7.8 million, and John Thomas Hayes paid $6.2 million for a 2022-built waterfront home at 3701 Northeast 26th Avenue in Lighthouse Point.

items.title: Kolter and Carlyle's 336-Unit One Alton Biscayne Tops Permits; Neumann's Flow and Huizenga File Demolitions
items.summary: For permits issued August 12-19, the largest was One Alton Biscayne, a 12-story, 336-unit apartment building at 11240 Biscayne Boulevard near North Miami from Kolter Multifamily, the Carlyle Group and Altman. The partners bought the site last year for $15 million and secured an $86.1 million construction loan from PNC Bank. On the demolition side, Huizenga Holdings - led by H. Wayne Huizenga Jr. - pulled seven permits across a West Palm Beach residential assemblage, Crescent Heights cleared the way for phase two of its 42-story Forma Suites tower in Miami's Edgewater, and Adam Neumann's Flow filed to demolish structures on the 16-acre former trailer park at 8500 Biscayne Boulevard it bought at a court-ordered auction for $70.5 million.

items.title: Palm Beach's 206 Phipps Plaza, a 1920s John Volk Design, Sells for $27.5M
items.summary: A company managed by Thomas J. Morrison sold the 6,900 SF house at 206 Phipps Plaza in Palm Beach to a trust for $27.5 million - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale. The seven-bedroom, nine-and-a-half-bath residence dates to the 1920s and once belonged to Palm Beach society architect John Volk; Jim McCann of Premier Estate Properties had the listing and Christopher Leavitt of Douglas Elliman represented the buyer. Also recorded that day: a 5,100 SF oceanfront home at 3567 South Ocean Boulevard in Highland Beach for $12.8 million - medical-technology executive Alexis Lukianov and his wife Katherine sold to Jonathan and Chemai Jura after first asking $15.9 million in October - plus a 5,000 SF villa at the Oceana Key Biscayne, 111 Reef Lane, for $10.9 million and a Miami Beach waterfront house at 5000 North Bay Road for $9.3 million.

items.title: U.S. Home-Sale Cancellations Hit Highest Level Since 2023; 14% of July Deals Fell Through
items.summary: Buyers backed out of just over 14 percent of pending U.S. home sales in July, the highest share since June 2023, according to Redfin data. More than 47,000 contracts were canceled nationwide during the month, a 4.8 percent year-over-year increase, though the cancellation share ran only 0.7 percentage points above July 2025. Southern markets, Florida among them, are posting the highest fall-through rates. The practical read for sellers: a signed contract is a weaker signal than it was two years ago - buyer diligence, insurance quotes and appraisal gaps are all live risks - so pricing to a realistic close rather than a headline list price matters more than it did in the 2021-22 market.

items.title: Bay Harbor Islands Waterfront Home Sells for $20M, Up from $12M in 2021
items.summary: Venture capitalist Fued Sadala and his wife Silvana sold their 5,900 SF waterfront home at 9814 West Broadview Drive in Bay Harbor Islands for $20 million - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale - to Jack Tabacinic, a managing director at Loom Capital Management, and Andrea Blau Russ. The 2002-built, five-bedroom house had been listed earlier in August at $22 million; the Sadalas paid $12 million for it in 2021, a roughly 67 percent gain in five years. Joel Lusky and Shneur Shapira of The Brokerage South Florida Real Estate represented both sides. Also recorded: a waterfront home at 4216 Intracoastal Drive in Highland Beach for $9.5 million, sold by hedge-fund manager Leonard Zelin and Moira Zelin to Antonio and Dolores Seabra, and a newly built home at 256 Alhambra Place in West Palm Beach for $7.5 million.

items.title: Florida Home Sales Rise for 11th Straight Month; Statewide Single-Family Median Hits $425,000
items.summary: July 2026 data released August 17 shows Florida's housing market posting its 11th consecutive month of year-over-year closed-sales gains in both major property types. Statewide single-family closings totaled 23,870, up 5.1%, while condo-townhouse sales totaled 8,194, up 11%. The statewide single-family median rose 3.7% to $425,000; the condo-townhouse median held flat at $295,000. Single-family inventory fell 13.4% to 97,741 active listings - a 4.5-months supply, squarely a seller's market - while condo supply sits at 7.8 months. Southeast Florida ran ahead of the state on price: Miami-Dade single-family median $685,000 (+3.8%), Broward $650,000 (+4.8%), Palm Beach $660,090 (+7.6%), with single-family active listings down 22.8%, 25.0% and 23.3% respectively. Million-dollar-plus sales climbed 15.5% in Miami-Dade and 33.9% in Broward.

items.title: Florida's November Property-Tax Amendment Draws Organized Opposition
items.summary: Amendment 3 on Florida's November ballot would raise the non-school homestead exemption from $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 by 2028, and would cut the annual cap on assessment increases for non-homestead property from 10% to 5%. It needs 60% voter approval. Legislative fiscal analysis estimates local government revenue would fall roughly $4.6 billion in the first year and $8.4 billion in the second, with no funding mechanism specified. Three political committees organized to oppose it - including Vote No on 3, also called Stop Unfair Tax Shifts - have together raised under $30,000 since the start of June, arguing the measure shifts the burden onto renters, commercial property owners and first-time buyers. For income-property owners the line item to watch is the non-homestead assessment cap: dropping it to 5% would materially slow taxable-value growth on rentals and small commercial assets.

items.title: Artemis Pays $140M for Delray Beach Senior-Living Community; Golden Beach Oceanfront Lot Fetches $24M
items.summary: An entity tied to Chevy Chase, Maryland-based Artemis Real Estate Partners bought a senior-living community at 6589 and 6595 Morikami Park Road in Delray Beach for $140 million from an affiliate of PGIM Real Estate - among the largest assisted-living trades ever recorded in Florida and the week's priciest South Florida commercial sale. The 2023-built complex spans 225,000 SF on 7.2 acres and holds 207 residences: 70 assisted-living, 76 independent-living and 41 memory-care units, with average monthly resident rates around $7,635. The week's top recorded home sale was dirt, not a house: a 0.6-acre oceanfront lot at 625 Ocean Boulevard in Golden Beach traded for $24 million, sold by the estate of Sydell Herrick to a company managed by spec developer David Rodriguez, who plans to build on the site.

items.title: Ken Griffin Sells Palm Beach's 125 Worth Avenue to Blackstone Affiliate for $86M
items.summary: Citadel founder Ken Griffin sold his 50,000 SF office building at 125 Worth Avenue in Palm Beach to Blackstone's Revantage for $86 million - the week's priciest recorded South Florida commercial deal. Griffin had paid $83 million for the Worth Avenue property in 2023, and the resale underscores how tightly held - and how institutionally sought after - trophy office space on Palm Beach's premier retail corridor has become as financial firms continue relocating to the island. The week's second-largest commercial trade was industrial: a 120,700 SF warehouse at 16175 Northwest 49th Avenue in Hialeah sold for $31 million, or nearly $257 per square foot, with Kurv Industrial selling to an entity tied to Salt Lake City-based Alsco Uniforms after buying it for $26.3 million in 2022.

items.title: Miami Beach's 508 West Dilido Flips for $22.8M, Six Months After a $18.5M Purchase
items.summary: A 5,500 SF waterfront home at 508 West Dilido Drive on Miami Beach's Venetian Islands sold for $22.8 million - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale. The 508 W Dilido Drive Land Trust sold to the 508 Di Lido Land Trust after paying $18.5 million for the 2018-built house in February of this year, a roughly 23% gain in about six months. Reid Heidenry and Marko Gojanovic of One Sotheby's International Realty represented the seller and Hayley Dodge of Compass brought the buyer. Quick resales at a premium remain a recurring feature of the Venetian and Sunset Islands market, where finished new-construction inventory is scarce.

items.title: Rilea's $85.6M Mohawk at Wynwood Tops South Florida Construction Permits
items.summary: South Florida's largest construction permit for the week ending August 10 was an $85.6 million new-building permit for Mohawk at Wynwood, Rilea Group's 300-unit, 488,880 SF apartment project at 50 Northeast 29th Street in Miami, which will include 30,000 SF of ground-floor retail and deliver in 2028. Rilea, led by Alan and Diego Ojeda, bought the land for $22 million in 2021 and closed a $149.2 million construction loan in January that included $124.2 million of C-PACE financing from Nuveen Green Capital. Also permitted: a $31.1 million, 115,820 SF permit for Sweetbird North, an eight-story office-and-retail project at 95 Northeast 40th Street from Miami Design District Associates and Raycliff Capital, and a $28 million permit for Kolter Multifamily's 336-unit Alton Biscayne at 11240 Biscayne Boulevard in North Miami Beach.

items.title: Mortgage Rates Post First Drop in Six Weeks to 6.67%; 15-Yr Falls to 5.96%
items.summary: Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 6.67% the week of August 13, down from 6.69% - its first weekly decline in six weeks - while the 15-year fixed fell to 5.96% from 6.01%. A year ago the 30-year FRM averaged 6.58%, leaving financing only marginally above year-ago levels. Chief economist Sam Khater said the modest pullback, combined with for-sale inventory that keeps improving and listing prices running slightly below a year ago, is gradually shifting conditions toward buyers. Bankrate/Mortgage Research Center pegged the 30-year jumbo average near 6.84% as of mid-August.

items.title: Moishe Mana's Mana Common Buys Downtown Miami Former Post Office for $20.3M; Key Biscayne Home Sells for $14M
items.summary: Affiliates of Miami-based Stambul sold a five-story former post office at 100 Northeast First Avenue in downtown Miami, plus a neighboring 15,000 SF vacant lot at 54 Northeast 2nd Street, to Moishe Mana's Mana Common for $20.3 million - the week's priciest recorded South Florida commercial deal and another piece of Mana's long-running downtown Miami land assemblage (the office building spans about 35,600 SF). The week's top recorded home sale was in Key Biscayne, where an entity led by Concha Dominguez sold a 4,300 SF waterfront residence at 591 North Mashta Drive for $14 million - about $3,300 per square foot - to a company managed by Alvaro Castro Mendivil; the seller had paid just $3.2 million for the property in 2004.

items.title: Palm Beach's Seabreeze Estate Sells for $17.1M to Red Ventures CEO; Fort Lauderdale Home Fetches $16M
items.summary: Ric Elias, co-founder and CEO of Red Ventures, and his wife, Brenda, paid $17.1 million for a 4,900 SF home at 350 Seabreeze Avenue in Palm Beach - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale. Seller Steven K. Hudson had bought the property for $15.8 million just three months earlier, in May (Christopher Leavitt held the listing and Jack Rooney brought the buyer, both of Douglas Elliman). In Fort Lauderdale, a 7,000 SF home at 1721 Southeast 11th Street - listed at $24.9 million a year ago - sold for $16 million, with an entity tied to Alon Steiger selling to Arlene G. Inch, chairwoman and owner of TransPak.

items.title: Aviation Exec Pays $19M for Surf Club Four Seasons Condo in Surfside
items.summary: Private-aviation executive William Papariella and accountant Michael Deo paid $19 million, through an LLC, for unit 307 in the south tower of the Four Seasons Residences at the Surf Club at 9001 Collins Avenue in Surfside - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale. The 4,000 SF, four-bedroom, four-and-a-half-bath condo traded for about $4,800 per square foot. The seller, a trust tied to Richard Gold that had paid $10.4 million for the unit in 2021, realized an 83% gain in five years - a mark of how durable trophy oceanfront-condo pricing has been across Miami-Dade's barrier-island market.

items.title: MLG Sells Lake Worth's Savona Grand Apartments for $64.8M; Holman Sheds FTL Honda Dealership for $44.8M
items.summary: Affiliates of Wisconsin-based MLG Legacy Fund Investments sold Savona Grand, a garden-style apartment community at 7132 Colony Club Drive in Lake Worth, for $64.8 million - the week's top recorded South Florida commercial trade and a sign of continued institutional appetite for stabilized Palm Beach County rentals. Holman Automotive shed the Stoler Honda of Fort Lauderdale dealership at 12 East Sunrise Boulevard - about 96,000 SF of buildings - for $44.8 million, and the week's priciest recorded home sale was in Hillsboro Beach, where auto-industry executive Mike Manley sold a 9,000 SF oceanfront house at 955 Hillsboro Mile for $14.5 million.

items.title: Starwood Buys Two Miami-Dade Affordable Housing Communities for $63.8M
items.summary: Barry Sternlicht's Starwood Asset Management paid a combined $63.8 million for two Miami-Dade affordable-housing rental communities, buying from the Gatehouse Group. Starwood paid $34 million for Magnolia Landing, a 150-unit, 20-building complex built in 2011 on 4.8 acres at 25881 Southwest 143rd Court in the Naranja area, and $29.75 million for Lafayette Square, a 160-unit, 19-story building on 1.2 acres at 150 Northeast 79th Street in Miami's Little River neighborhood. CBRE Capital Markets arranged a $23.8 million Freddie Mac loan for the deal, which underscores growing institutional appetite for income-restricted rentals as market-rate multifamily activity moderates.
items.source: Commercial Observer / Commercial Real Estate Direct

items.title: Witkoff's $97M Shore Club, Related's Gallery at Lummus Top South Florida Permits
items.summary: South Florida's largest construction permits for the week ending August 5 were led by a $97 million phased new-construction permit for The Shore Club Private Collection at 1901 Collins Avenue in Miami Beach - Witkoff and Monroe Capital's roughly 481,200 SF luxury condo-and-hotel project (about 45 residences and 79 hotel rooms), which lined up $430 million in construction financing in 2023. The second-largest was a $74.5 million permit for the Related Group's Gallery at Lummus, a 415,500 SF apartment project at 395 Northwest First Street in Miami. The pipeline highlights how ultra-luxury coastal condos and large rental towers continue to drive the region's development activity.

items.title: Rivani Buys Miami Beach's 404 Washington Office-Retail Building for $31.5M
items.summary: Local developer Rivani paid $31.5 million - about $201 per square foot - for 404 Washington, a 156,752 SF office-and-retail building in Miami Beach, buying from Dominion Partners LP of Sunny Isles Beach. The purchase reflects continued investor interest in well-located South Beach commercial space even as broader South Florida office and retail sales volume cooled in the first half of 2026.
items.source: Commercial Real Estate Direct / South Florida Business Journal

items.title: Fisher Island Condo Sells for $15M; Margate Medical Complex Trades for $14.7M
items.summary: Software executive Mark Sutcliffe paid $15 million for a 3,600 SF condo at 7811 Fisher Island Drive in Miami - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale (three bedrooms, three-and-a-half baths, plus about 2,100 SF of terraces), buying from a company led by Olga Postolnikov. Also trading was a Miami home at 7426 Southwest 49th Place, which a trust bought for $9.3 million from entrepreneur Juan Tavares and Naila Gonzalez. The region's priciest recorded commercial deal was a Margate medical-office complex at 3251 and 3271-3285 North State Road 7, which changed hands for $14.7 million.

items.title: Miami's Kiaora Street New-Build Sells for $22.5M; Harbor Group Pays $109M for a SoFla Property
items.summary: A trust paid $22.5 million for a newly built 8,500 SF home at 4040 Kiaora Street in Miami - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale (six bedrooms, seven-and-a-half baths, with a guest house). Other notable trades included a $9.9 million Fort Lauderdale waterfront home at 4 Isla Bahia Drive, bought by Andrea Naticchione, and an $18 million vacant waterfront lot at 10312 West Broadview Drive in Bay Harbor Islands, which a family trust sold to an affiliate of David Burstyn's Winston Capital Management. In the week's top commercial deal, Norfolk, Virginia-based Harbor Group International paid $109 million for a South Florida commercial property.

items.title: Bal Harbour Oceanfront Condo Sells for $14.5M to Lead the Week's Deals
items.summary: A trust paid $14.5 million - about $3,600 per square foot - for a 4,000 SF oceanfront corner condo at 10201 Collins Avenue in Bal Harbour, the week's top recorded South Florida home sale (three bedrooms, four-and-a-half baths, with a terrace and ocean views), buying from a company led by Jason Claxton. The week's priciest commercial deal was in Lantana, where Miami-based Cherry Oak Management sold an assisted-living facility at 6026 Old Congress Road for $8.4 million. Also trading: a Lauderhill shopping center at 7100-7200 West Commercial Boulevard that sold for $6.8 million, from an entity tied to investor Allen Chelminsky.

items.title: Pinecrest Development Lot Sells for $14.5M; Doral Dealership Site Trades for $23M
items.summary: Financier Mauro Ivan Korlaet Araya and lifestyle-and-fashion influencer Daniela Fernandez Nazer paid $14.5 million for a vacant 1.1-acre lot at 9601 Southwest 67th Avenue in Pinecrest - the week's top recorded South Florida residential deal, a land price that underscores how scarce large buildable parcels have become in the affluent village. The week's most expensive commercial sale was a used-car dealership property at 8505 Northwest 12th Street in Doral, which changed hands for $23 million, reflecting continued investor demand for infill Miami-Dade commercial land.

items.title: Hallandale Beach's Millennium Plaza Mixed-Use Property Trades for $40M
items.summary: AS Hallandale Investment FL paid $40 million - about $209 per square foot - for Millennium Plaza, a 191,084 SF mixed-use retail-and-office property at 2500 East Hallandale Beach Boulevard in Hallandale Beach, roughly 14 miles south of Fort Lauderdale. The purchase adds to a wave of capital targeting Hallandale Beach, a dense, transit-adjacent submarket between Fort Lauderdale and Miami where developers have been assembling sites for mixed-use and residential redevelopment. Necessity-oriented, infill commercial assets in built-out coastal Broward continue to trade even as broader South Florida commercial volume cooled in the first half of 2026.

items.title: Boca Raton's Royal Palm Estate Sells for $21.5M; Willow Bridge Buys Fort Lauderdale Dev Site for $24.7M
items.summary: A trust paid $21.5 million for a newly built 9,400 SF home at 1642 Sabal Palm Drive in Boca Raton's Royal Palm Yacht and Country Club - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale (seven bedrooms, eight-and-a-half baths). Sellers John and Mary Hargrove had paid $6 million for it a year earlier, and it last asked just under $23 million (David Roberts of Royal Palm Properties held the listing; Douglas Elliman brought the buyer). The top commercial deal was a Fort Lauderdale development site at 1040 Bayview Drive, which an affiliate of Atlanta-based Willow Bridge Property Company bought for $24.7 million from a Procacci Development Corporation entity that had filed plans for a 259-unit mixed-use project. Also closing: a $9.3 million Miami two-home lot at 1650 Micanopy Avenue and an $8.2 million Opa-locka auto-services facility sold by a Longpoint Realty affiliate.

items.title: CIP Real Estate Pays $99M for Coconut Creek's Lyons Corporate Park
items.summary: CIP Real Estate paid $99 million - about $293 per square foot - for Lyons Corporate Park, a 337,392 SF multi-building industrial park at 6601 Lyons Road in Coconut Creek, roughly seven miles southwest of Boca Raton, buying from Industrial Development Co. and Lyons Corporate Park Co. LLLP. It was among South Florida's largest commercial trades of the week and reinforces how infill, shallow-bay industrial remains the region's most sought-after commercial asset class even as multifamily, office and retail sales volume cooled in the first half of 2026. Separately, the week's priciest recorded home sale was a newly built 6,900 SF house at 340 San Marco Drive in Fort Lauderdale that traded for $9.5 million (about $1,400 per square foot), sold by an entity tied to MDS Energy Development CEO Michael Snyder.
items.source: Commercial Real Estate Direct / The Real Deal

items.title: Kimco Realty Buys Two Broward Grocery-Anchored Centers for $109M
items.summary: Kimco Realty paid $109 million for two grocery-anchored Broward shopping centers, buying from KPR Centers. The larger deal was Sunshine Plaza, a 245,744 SF Publix- and Marshalls-anchored center on about 19 acres at 4017-4299 West Commercial Boulevard in Tamarac, for $56 million. Kimco paid $53 million for Pompano Marketplace, a 254,749 SF center at 1115-1117 South Federal Highway anchored by a Walmart Neighborhood Market. The purchases extend the REIT's push into necessity-based, grocery-anchored retail in dense South Florida submarkets - a segment that has held its value even as broader commercial volume cooled in the first half.

items.title: Mortgage Rates Rise to 6.69%; 15-Yr Eases to 6.01%
items.summary: Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 6.69% the week of August 6, up from 6.66% and extending its summer climb, while the 15-year fixed edged down to 6.01% from 6.04%. A year ago the 30-year FRM averaged 6.63%, so financing now sits marginally above year-ago levels. Chief economist Sam Khater noted listing prices are running modestly below year-ago levels and for-sale inventory continues to improve from the tight supply of recent years - a gradual shift toward buyers. Bankrate's 30-year jumbo average was about 6.90% as of early August.

items.title: Skechers Co-Founder Buys $10.5M Miami Home; Julia Hotel Trades for $9.1M
items.summary: Skechers co-founder Michael Greenberg, through an LLC, bought a 3,400 SF home at 3600 Stewart Avenue in Miami for $10.5 million - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale (four bedrooms, three-and-a-half baths). Sellers Roberta Manelli and Francisco Salonia-Ruzo had paid $2.1 million for the property in 2015. The week's top commercial deal was the Julia Hotel at 336 Collins Avenue in Miami Beach, which an affiliate of Miami-based SMS Lodging sold for $9.1 million - about $314,000 per key - to C&D Bay Village LLC, managed by investors Danilo Damolin and Lorenzo Costa.

items.title: Baptist Hospital $45M Expansion, Ritz-Carlton South Beach Top Miami-Area Permits
items.summary: South Florida's largest construction permits for the week ending July 29 were led by a $45 million interior-alteration permit for Baptist Health South Florida's 111,500 SF expansion of Baptist Hospital Miami at 8900 North Kendall Drive, followed by a $43.6 million, 36,700 SF renovation of the Brickell East condominium at 151 Southeast 15th Road. The largest new-construction permits were $28.4 million for phased work at the Ritz-Carlton, South Beach at 1 Lincoln Road in Miami Beach and $18 million for The Cove at 1055 North Federal Highway in Fort Lauderdale - Affiliated Development's eight-story, 376-unit Live Local Act rental, which recently landed a $74 million construction loan from Pacific Life.

items.title: Kamson, Scopus Buy 400-Unit West Palm Beach Rental Community for $90.5M
items.summary: A joint venture of the Kamson Corporation and Joel Gluck's Scopus Property Management paid $90.5 million - about $226,250 per unit - for Ponte Verde at Palm Beach Lakes, a 400-unit garden-style rental community on roughly 28 acres at 1401 Village Boulevard in West Palm Beach. Built in 1990 as apartments, the 23-building, ~360,500 SF property was converted to condominiums and then restored to rental housing in August 2025. Prospect Ridge and Blue Owl provided an $81 million acquisition loan. The trade was among South Florida's largest multifamily deals of the summer and underscores continued institutional appetite for well-located, workforce-oriented rentals in Palm Beach County.
items.source: The Real Deal / Commercial Real Estate Direct

items.title: Integra Buys Condemned 304-Unit Pembroke Pines Condo Complex for $20.5M
items.summary: Miami-based Integra Investments acquired Heron Pond - a vacant 304-unit, 19-building condominium community at 8320 Southwest 1st Street in Pembroke Pines - for $20.5 million through a court-appointed receivership auction, closing a legal battle after a bulk-unit owner's challenge was denied. Built in 1988 as apartments and converted to condos in 2000, the complex has sat empty since the city declared it unsafe and evacuated residents in 2024 over termite damage, rotted beams and wind-resistance defects. In-place zoning allows up to 321 units by right and the count could more than double through upzoning - a large-scale value-add/redevelopment play in western Broward.

items.title: Waste Management Pays $379M for Medley Landfill Site in Week's Top Commercial Deal
items.summary: Waste Management Inc. paid $379.4 million for a 146-acre, largely vacant industrial site near Northwest 95th Avenue and Northwest 106th Street in Medley - buying from a company managed by Lowell and Loretta Dunn and planning to use it as a landfill - South Florida's largest recorded commercial deal of the week. Also trading: HarborChase of Boynton Beach, a 120,000 SF senior-living community built in 2023, sold for just under $35 million (a Lotis-Chaudhary Development Group affiliate to LA-based Range Equity Management), and a WareSpace affiliate bought a 119,000 SF Medley industrial building from a Blackstone/Link Logistics entity for $15 million ($126 per square foot).

items.title: Miami Beach Penthouse Sells for $23.5M to Lead the Week's Home Deals
items.summary: A trust tied to Yves Mongeau and Sylvie Guilbault sold a 9,000 SF penthouse at 450 Alton Road in Miami Beach for $23.5 million - about $2,600 per square foot - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale (six bedrooms, seven-and-a-half baths; the sellers had paid $15 million in 2013, last asking $28.9 million), with Akron Warwick Exchange LLC buying. In Surfside, fashion designer Tomas Maier and Andrew Preston sold a Surf Club Four Seasons condo at 9111 Collins Avenue for $17.7 million, or $5,900 per square foot, after paying $13 million in 2023.

items.title: West Palm Beach's Alba Sponsor Unit Sells for $10.4M to Lead the Week's Deals
items.summary: David Goulden and Andrea Helen McDonough bought a sponsor unit at the new Alba Palm Beach condominium at 4714 North Flagler Drive in West Palm Beach for $10.4 million - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale (a five-bedroom, five-bathroom residence of about 4,500 square feet). The top commercial deal of the week was in Medley, where Miami-based developer Tekton Development paid $6.6 million for an industrial property, underscoring continued institutional appetite for infill Miami-Dade logistics real estate even through the slow summer season.

items.title: Mortgage Rates Extend Climb to 6.66%; 15-Yr Rises to 6.04%
items.summary: Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed averaged 6.66% the week of July 30, up from 6.58% and marking a fourth consecutive weekly increase (6.49% on July 9, 6.55%, 6.58%, now 6.66%). The 15-year fixed rose to 6.04% from 5.96%. A year ago the 30-year FRM averaged 6.72%, so financing remains modestly cheaper than 2025, and Freddie Mac notes rising inventory continues to improve affordability for buyers who stay engaged even as purchase demand softens. Bankrate's 30-year jumbo average was about 6.85% as of July 30.

items.title: South Florida Luxury Price Threshold Jumps to $3.3M; Ultra-Luxury Hits $10.7M
items.summary: MIAMI REALTORS chief economist Gay Cororaton reports South Florida's single-family luxury (top 5% of sales) price threshold climbed to $3.3 million in the first half of 2026, up from $2.7 million in 2025, while the ultra-luxury (top 1%) threshold jumped to $10.7 million from $7.8 million - highest in Miami-Dade ($15M), Palm Beach ($14M) and Martin ($10.5M). The condo luxury threshold rose to $2.3 million and ultra-luxury to $6.0 million. Out-of-state buyers grew to 10% of domestic buyers (from 7% in 2024-25), led by New York (34%), New Jersey (13%) and California (8%), and bought at higher price points - California's single-family luxury threshold was $8.5 million.

items.title: Bal Harbour Oceana Penthouse Sells for $20.9M to Lead the Week's Deals
items.summary: A roughly 5,000 SF penthouse at the Oceana Bal Harbour, 10201 Collins Avenue, sold for $20.9 million to Oceana PH2802 Holdings LLC - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale (three bedrooms, five-and-a-half baths; the selling trust had paid $22 million for the unit in 2023). In Palm Beach County, Charles and Alexandra Prakas paid $5.7 million for a roughly 5,400 SF, five-bedroom home at 619 Riverside Road in North Palm Beach. The steady stream of eight-figure closings underscores how the ultra-luxury market keeps clearing through the slow summer season.

items.title: West Palm Beach Mansion Sells for $15.7M, Shattering the City's Non-Waterfront Record
items.summary: A newly built 8,600 SF mansion at 122 Bloomfield Drive in West Palm Beach sold for $15.7 million - about $1,820 per square foot - breaking the city's record for the priciest non-waterfront home sale (the prior record was $9 million in 2024). 122 Bloomfield Trust, managed by Francis Lynch, bought from an entity tied to financier Mark Marcello, who had paid $2.9 million for the lot in 2024. Broker Margit Brandt noted coastal West Palm homes now fetch $1,500-$2,000 per foot - a relative bargain versus Palm Beach island's $3,000-$4,000 - as buyers chase inland space and lower insurance costs; inland luxury set a record last year with 123 deals totaling $2.12 billion.

items.title: Swire's $240M Mandarin Oriental Tower Tops South Florida Construction Permits
items.summary: The week's largest South Florida construction permit was a $240 million filing for 1 Island Drive on Brickell Key, where Swire Properties is building The Residences at Mandarin Oriental, Miami and a Mandarin Oriental hotel totaling about 1.35 million square feet of condos and hotel. Ranking second was a $95 million permit for Sense 22 at 114 Northeast 22nd Street in Miami - New Sense LLC's Live Local Act mixed-use project of roughly 503,000 SF rising 36 stories with more than 320 units.

items.title: Ponce-Davis New-Build Mansion Sells for $18.9M; Moishe Mana Buys Wynwood's Pastis Building for $24.5M
items.summary: The priciest recorded South Florida home sale of the week was a roughly 10,000 SF new-construction mansion at 5545 Southwest 81st Terrace in Miami's Ponce-Davis neighborhood, which traded for $18.9 million - an LLC managed by Christophe Scherman selling to an entity led by telecommunications executive Meinrad Spenger (nearly 1-acre lot, seven bedrooms, guest house; last asked $22 million). The top commercial deal was also in Miami: developer Moishe Mana paid $24.5 million for the 13,000 SF Wynwood buildings at 380 and 320 Northwest 26th Street, home to Pastis and Apparatus, from a New York company tied to David Edelstein. Elsewhere, a Jupiter waterfront home at 9 Bamboo Lane sold for $10.5 million (about $1,500 per square foot) and a penthouse at the Alina in Boca Raton fetched $6.6 million.

items.title: South Florida Million-Dollar Sales Surge as Closed Sales Rise for a 10th Straight Month
items.summary: MIAMI REALTORS reports South Florida closed sales rose in June for the 10th consecutive month, at an 18.6% annual pace, with year-to-date sales up 7.9% - well ahead of the 2.2% national year-to-date gain. Year-to-date single-family sales are up 9.0% across every county: Palm Beach (+11.4%), Miami-Dade (+9.5%), Broward (+7.2%), Martin (+17.2%) and St. Lucie (+3.2%). The luxury tier is leading: the region logged 3,382 million-dollar transactions in Q1 2026, up 22% year over year, with million-dollar single-family sales up 26.7%. Driver-license exchanges - a proxy for out-of-state migration, largely from New York and California - rose 16% year over year in the first half.

items.title: Jupiter Bear's Club Mansion Sells for $33.8M; Wellington Senior-Living Facility Trades for $30.7M
items.summary: Spec developer Stuart Hankin sold a newly completed 10,900 SF mansion at 228 Bear's Club Drive in Jupiter for $33.8 million to tech executive Derek Kreunen and Erin Kreunen - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale and a sharp markup on the $3.4 million Hankin paid for the lot in 2021 (six bedrooms, theater, pool). The top commercial deal was the Alamar Senior Living facility at 8785 Lake Worth Road in Wellington, which traded for $30.7 million as Chicago-based Walton Street Capital sold to an entity linked to Health Wave Partners. Also closing: a $24 million Boca Raton home at 1992 Royal Palm Way and a $21.6 million ocean-view condo at the Estates at Acqualina in Sunny Isles Beach.

items.title: Key Biscayne Waterfront Home Sells for $17.5M to Lead the Week's Deals
items.summary: A waterfront home at 230 Harbor Drive in Key Biscayne sold for $17.5 million, with Nozin chairman Philippe Touret parting with a property he had owned for decades (6,200+ SF, seven bedrooms; last asked $21.8 million). A Fort Lauderdale home at 8 Harborage Isle Drive followed at $13.7 million - about $1,500 per square foot - and a Palm Beach condo at 2 North Breakers Row, with a cabana unit included, traded for $12.1 million.

items.title: Venetian Islands Double Waterfront Trades for $33M; Miami's 790 Lake Road Fetches $27.3M
items.summary: A trust sold two neighboring 1940s-built waterfront homes at 617 and 625 East Dilido Drive on Miami Beach's Venetian Islands for $33 million (0.7 acres; roughly 5,000 and 4,400 SF) to Leet House 4 LLC - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale. In Miami, a 6,100 SF waterfront home at 790 Lake Road traded for $27.3 million, about $6,700 per square foot (an entity tied to Adonel Concrete CEO Luis Garcia selling; last asked $32 million), and a Wellington equestrian estate at 12940 50th Street with barn space sold for $23 million. On the commercial side, a ~56,300 SF Deerfield Beach warehouse at 1143 West Newport Center Drive sold for $10.6 million.

items.title: Mortgage Rates Rise a Second Straight Week: 30-Yr Fixed 6.55%, 15-Yr 5.93%
items.summary: Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed averaged 6.55% the week of July 16, up from 6.49% and marking a second consecutive weekly increase. The 15-year jumped 11 basis points to 5.93%. A year ago the 30-year FRM was 6.75%, so financing is still cheaper than 2025, and Freddie Mac notes affordability is improving as inventory rises even though purchase-application demand has softened. Bankrate's 30-year jumbo average was 6.63% as of July 15.

items.title: South Florida Commercial Sales Fall 13% to $5.42B in H1 2026 - But Construction Is the Most Intense in the Nation
items.summary: MIAMI REALTORS chief economist Gay Cororaton reports South Florida commercial sales volume fell 13% year over year to $5.42 billion in the first half of 2026 amid geopolitical tensions and macro risk. Volume dropped for multifamily (-12%), office (-32%) and retail (-15%) but rose for industrial (+2%); multifamily still led at $1.95 billion, ahead of industrial ($1.54B), retail ($1.02B) and office ($910M). Broward led counties at $2.35 billion (+7%), ahead of Miami-Dade ($2.05B, -28%) and Palm Beach ($880M, -15%). Pricing held up - median price per building SF rose 1.0% to $330, with retail +24%, office +12% and industrial +7% but multifamily -3%. Fundamentals remain strong: Miami-Dade has 19,131 multifamily units under construction (9.7% of inventory vs 3.5% nationally), and the West Palm Beach-Boca Raton office market has 2.4M SF underway, adding 5.2% to stock - the most intense in the country.

items.title: Sean Combs Sells Star Island Estate for $55M, Leading the Week's Home Deals
items.summary: Sean Combs sold the 8,000 SF, six-bedroom estate at 1 Star Island Drive in Miami Beach for $55 million to JFStar LLC, led by John A. Franklin of Virginia Beach - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale and a $20 million step up from the $35 million he paid in 2021. Also closing: a $8.5M Boca Raton home on West Coconut Palm Road, a $7.9M Jupiter waterfront on Spyglass Lane, and a Sunny Isles Beach condo at $1,500 per square foot.

items.title: Venetian Islands Home Doubles to $42.5M; Royal-Linked Palm Beach Estate Fetches $31.8M
items.summary: A 2025-built waterfront home at 416 West San Marino Drive on Miami Beach's Venetian Islands traded for $42.5 million - nearly double the $23.1 million it fetched in 2024 - with Long Light Capital CEO Justin Korsant selling. In Palm Beach, a trust tied to the late Prince Albrecht of Oettingen-Spielberg sold the oceanfront home at 143 East Inlet Drive for $31.8 million after decades of family ownership, while Coral Gables saw a $24.5M Casuarina Concourse mansion and a $20.5M Balada Street sale by a trust tied to former Tinder CEO Gregory Blatt.

items.title: Longpoint Pays $24.6M for 90K SF Miami Warehouse Complex in Week's Top Commercial Deal
items.summary: A two-building warehouse complex at 8452 Northwest 72nd Street in Miami spanning nearly 90,000 SF sold for $24.6 million - about $273 per square foot - with a trust selling to an affiliate of Boston-based Longpoint. Institutional industrial buyers continue to pay up for infill Miami-Dade logistics product.

items.title: REITs Outperform the Broader Market in H1 2026 on Strong Operating Fundamentals
items.summary: The Nareit All Equity REIT index posted total returns of nearly 15% across the first and second quarters of 2026, beating the Russell 1000 (10.3%) and the S&P 500 (10.2%) despite elevated interest rates - a signal that property-level cash flows, not cheap debt, are driving real estate returns this cycle.

items.title: Palm Island Double-Lot Estate Sells for $40M, Leading the Week's Home Deals
items.summary: Homebuilder Adrian Pedro sold a double-lot estate at 145-149 Palm Avenue on Miami Beach's Palm Island for $40 million to venture investor Ben Ling and Hedge Labs co-founder Christopher Coudron - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale. The property, with a pool, cabana and tennis court, had listed in September asking $59 million; the buyers already own the neighboring mansion.

items.title: Mortgage Rates Tick Back Up: 30-Yr Fixed 6.49%, Jumbo 6.63%
items.summary: Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed averaged 6.49% the week of July 9, up from 6.43% and giving back last week's seven-week low, with the 15-year at 5.82%. Bankrate's 30-year jumbo average rose to 6.63% from 6.60%. A year ago the 30-year FRM was 6.72% - financing remains cheaper than 2025 despite the weekly uptick.

items.title: Sun Sentinel Printing Plant in Deerfield Beach Trades for $65M in Week's Top Commercial Deal
items.summary: The Sun Sentinel's ~382,000 SF printing-press industrial complex at 333 SW 12th Avenue in Deerfield Beach sold for $65 million, with Gramercy Property Trust exiting a site it bought a decade ago for $25.5 million. Also active: Dallas-based Tabani Group's $25.7M purchase of Miami's Wynwood Jungle retail complex and Hertz offloading three parking lots for $13.2 million.

items.title: $193M Miami Freedom Park Permit Tops South Florida Construction Filings
items.summary: The week's largest construction permit was a $193 million filing for Miami Freedom Park near Miami International Airport - a 1M+ SF retail, dining, office and hotel complex with 750 hotel rooms and a 58-acre public park anchored by Inter Miami's completed Nu Stadium. A $180 million permit for Cohen Brothers' West Palm Point office tower at 850 South Quadrille Boulevard in West Palm Beach ranked second.

items.title: Coral Gables Hospital ER Center Trades for $32M, Topping Week's Commercial Deals
items.summary: Coral Gables Hospital's off-campus emergency center at 8665 Bird Road in Miami sold for $32 million - an Amdur Management affiliate selling the nearly 8-acre site to an LLC managed by Supermarket Management. A day earlier, the ~37,000 SF Gun Club Shopping Center at 4645 Gun Club Road in West Palm Beach traded for $15 million.

items.title: Palm Beach $25M Sale Leads the Week; Pinecrest Mansion Fetches $17.5M
items.summary: A 7,200 SF, six-bedroom home at 239 Emerald Lane in Palm Beach sold for $25 million to Terakeet co-founder Mac Cummings, leading South Florida's recorded residential deals for the week. A Pinecrest mansion at 13291 Old Cutler Road followed at $17.5 million.

items.title: Surf Club Four Seasons Condo Asking $32M Tops a Slow Listing Week
items.summary: A condo at the Four Seasons Residences at The Surf Club in Surfside hit the market asking $32 million - the priciest new South Florida listing in an otherwise quiet holiday week, underscoring that trophy oceanfront resale supply is thin but pricing ambitiously.

items.title: Davie School Building Trades for $16M in Week's Top Commercial Deal
items.summary: A ~46,000 SF school building at 3367 North University Drive in Davie sold for $16 million to lead South Florida's recorded commercial deals for the week, while a Pinecrest home at 5865 SW 96th Street topped residential at $7.8 million and a newly built Boca Raton home traded at about $1,200 per square foot.

items.title: Bal Harbour Shops Expansion, Pinnacle Affordable Project Lead Top Permits
items.summary: The week's largest new building permit was an $11.8 million filing for Pinnacle's two-building Pinnacle at Cypress affordable-housing development at 6520 North Andrews Avenue in Fort Lauderdale, while Bal Harbour Shops' luxury retail expansion also ranked among South Florida's top construction permits.

items.title: Mortgage Rates Hit Seven-Week Low: 30-Yr Fixed at 6.43%, Jumbo 6.60%
items.summary: Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed averaged 6.43% the week of July 2, down from 6.49% and well below the 6.67% of a year ago, with the 15-year at 5.79%. Bankrate's 30-year jumbo average eased to 6.60% - a friendlier financing backdrop for SE Florida buyers heading into summer.

items.title: Florida Insurance Rate Cuts Take Effect July 1: Citizens -8.7% Statewide, SE FL Counties ~-14%
items.summary: Florida OIR-approved homeowners rate decreases took effect July 1 for new policies (and at renewal for existing ones). Citizens' average statewide decrease is about 8.7% - with Miami-Dade and Broward seeing cuts near 14% - while private carriers including State Farm (-10.1%) continue filing reductions. More than 15 new insurers have entered since the 2022-23 reforms.

items.title: Palm Beach $21M Sale Leads South Florida's Top Deals into July
items.summary: A ~6,000 SF Palm Beach home at 242 Wells Road traded for $21 million to lead the week's residential deals, joined by a $15.25M Jupiter Inlet beachfront closing, a $13.2M Lighthouse Point waterfront sale and a $10.5M La Gorce Circle sale in Miami Beach - the eight-figure market stayed busy straight into the summer.

items.title: Investor Lists $138M in Trophy Penthouses, Including $78M Miami Beach Unit
items.summary: Investor William Duker put two penthouses on the market for a combined $138 million - including a three-story unit at Miami Beach's Apogee at 800 South Pointe Drive asking $78 million, which would rank among the priciest condo listings in South Florida.

items.title: Florida Property-Insurance Cat Reinsurance Prices Fall 15-20% at June Renewals
items.summary: Guy Carpenter reports risk-adjusted Florida property-catastrophe reinsurance pricing down roughly 15-20% across many layers at the June 2026 renewals, easing a key cost driver for coastal-property carriers and, in turn, homeowner premiums.

items.title: Viceroy Brickell Completes as Villa Miami Climbs - Condo Pipeline Milestones
items.summary: The 45-story Viceroy Brickell - the brand's first fully residential tower - completed construction and is welcoming its first owners, while Villa Miami reached its 37th floor and The Residences at Mandarin Oriental opened its North Tower sales gallery.

items.title: Is South Florida's Branded-Condo Boom Reaching Its Limit?
items.summary: The Real Deal's June magazine examines growing saturation in South Florida's branded-condo market, where dozens of hotel- and designer-branded towers have turned a premium differentiator into the new normal - sharpening the focus on location and developer track record.

items.title: Waterfront Estate of Palm Beach's Oldest Resident Trades for $35M
items.summary: The 6,700 SF waterfront home at 350 Island Road - residence of Palm Beach's oldest resident for over six decades - sold for $35 million in an apparent all-cash deal, months after listing at $41 million. Island trophy product keeps clearing at scale even off peak ask.

items.title: Dezer Pivots to Broader Market With ~600-Unit North Miami Rental Project
items.summary: Dezer Development, long known for ultra-luxury branded condos, is planning nearly 600 market-rate apartments in North Miami - a notable signal that big South Florida developers see the deepest demand in attainable rental product.

items.title: Broward Beach Resort Headed to July 16 Foreclosure Auction Over $40M Debt
items.summary: The Hillsboro Beach Resort at 1159 Hillsboro Mile - a former Sonder property - is set for a July 16 foreclosure auction following a $26 million loan default, a reminder that pockets of hospitality distress persist even in a strong coastal market.

items.title: Colliers: South Florida Multifamily Cap Rates Hold Near 5.0%
items.summary: Colliers' Q1 2026 South Florida multifamily report shows cap rates steady near 5.0% as elevated insurance and operating costs shape pricing. Miami's vacancy is the lowest among major Florida metros at 6.6%, versus Orlando 7.3%, Tampa 8.8% and Jacksonville 12.2%.

items.title: Miami-Dade Home Sales Rise for Ninth Straight Month; SF Median at $680K
items.summary: May 2026 stats from MIAMI Realtors show total Miami-Dade home sales up 7.9% year-over-year - the ninth consecutive monthly gain - with $1M+ sales up 14.7% and the single-family median at $680,000 (+0.7%). Condo inventory fell 8.9%, its fourth straight monthly decline.

items.title: SE Florida Home Sales Up Year-Over-Year for Consecutive Spring Months
items.summary: Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach each posted higher total home sales year-over-year across consecutive spring months, signaling sustained tri-county momentum even as pricing cools from recent highs.

items.title: Palm Beach County Average Sale Price Climbs 11% YTD to $1.025M
items.summary: Palm Beach County's average sale price rose 11% year-to-date from $924,000 to just over $1,025,000, with the median up 3% to $518,500. An unusually high share of cash closings underscores that liquidity, not leverage, is setting the pace.

items.title: South Florida $1M+ Sales Up 22% in Q1 2026
items.summary: Sales of properties priced above $1 million across South Florida rose 22% in Q1 2026 versus a year earlier. In May, Miami-Dade million-dollar sales were up 14.7% year-over-year, extending a strong luxury run.

items.title: West Palm Beach Office Pipeline Tops 3.3M SF as Corporate Relocations Continue
items.summary: West Palm Beach has roughly 3.3 million SF of office space in the pipeline - nearly 700,000 SF under construction - as corporate relocations and financial-services migration cement the city as a regional commercial hub.
items.source: Discover South Florida / Markets of Tomorrow

items.title: Related Breaks Ground / Advances Marquee West Palm Beach Luxury Condos
items.summary: Related Cos. is advancing South Flagler House, and the Nora District marked the groundbreaking of a 201-key boutique hotel - part of a deep West Palm Beach luxury-condo and mixed-use pipeline delivering into 2026-2027.

items.title: Florida Statewide Single-Family Median Hits $425K, Up 2.4% YoY
items.summary: Florida Realtors' May 2026 data put the statewide single-family median at about $425,000, up 2.4% year-over-year, with closed sales rising for the ninth straight month as the market approached a summer inflection point.

items.title: Boca Raton Spec Mansion Asking $80M Poised to Shatter City Record
items.summary: An $80 million spec mansion leading Boca Raton contracts is positioned to set a new city price record, reflecting continued demand for turnkey, ultra-high-end waterfront product in southern Palm Beach County.

items.title: Florida Insurance Trends Shift Toward Relief; Citizens Down to ~395K Policies
items.summary: State-backed Citizens has fallen from 1.42 million policies in late 2023 to roughly 395,000 in January 2026 - the lowest since 2012 - as private carriers file rate decreases and take back risk. SE Florida counties are averaging 11-14% decreases.

items.title: Developer Sells Renovated Palm Beach Waterfront Home for $30.8M
items.summary: Developer Mosie Miller and his wife sold a renovated Palm Beach waterfront home for $30.8 million after more than a year on the market - a sign that even trophy assets are trading on positioning and pricing discipline.
